qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Deep switching costs in engineering workflows driven by proprietary automated test software scripts, calibration science, and standards-body integration. Proven by 63-65% gross margins and 14.2% 10-year median ROIC. Primary erosion threats include rapid technological obsolescence and modular/software-defined instrument alternatives.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Electronic test and measurement hardware faces severe cyclicality tied to telecom capex and semiconductor cycles, coupled with an active terminal headwind on Macrotrend 3 (Geopolitical Realignment & Supply Chain Reshoring). Expanding US export controls curb shipments of advanced test instruments to China (~17% revenue exposure), while Chinese state-mandated domestic substitution (Rigol, Siglent, Ceyear) permanently erodes addressable demand. High ongoing R&D treadmill (~16% of sales) required to counter rapid technological obsolescence caps CAP below the 15-year hurdle.
qualitative.evidence: Spun off from Agilent in 2014 with HP heritage dating to 1939. Generates ~63-65% gross margins with a 10-year median ROIC of 14.2% (5-year average ~15.5%). Highly cyclical end markets: revenue declined from $5.46B in FY22 to $4.98B in FY24 following the post-5G capex contraction before recovering to ~$5.4B in FY25. High customer switching costs in lab automated test environments, but heavily exposed to China (~15-20% of sales) and geopolitical export bans on advanced RF/semiconductor test tools. FCF conversion historically strong (~80-100% of net income) with net debt / EBITDA < 1.0x, but runway longevity is constrained by rapid tech obsolescence and geopolitical fragmentation.
